decisions.reason: After only one year there is still substantial uncertainty, and a decorative carpet is a relatively low-commitment option to keep on offer while demand information accumulates.
The premium hand-knotted wool-silk carpet is a niche but potentially high-value option, so we would keep it for now despite a somewhat higher pruning risk if it fails to prove its appeal soon.
Like the other low-pile decorative rug, it is still early to judge and the cost of preserving the option is likely low compared with the value of learning from another selling period.
A corner bench fits the core furniture business closely, so with no negative signal yet we would continue to support it and wait for clearer evidence before abandoning it.
This more generic low-pile carpet faces the highest portfolio overlap risk, but we would still keep it one more year because uncertainty remains and carrying the option is likely inexpensive.
A swivel shell chair is a core furniture-category product with plausible customer fit, so real-options logic favors keeping it on the market until performance becomes clearer.
